plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in temperate climates with cold winters and is a classic feature of cottage gardens and old homesteads.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; widely cultivated across North America, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Lilacs can live for over 100 years and often persist at abandoned homesites long after the buildings are gone.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, showy, often fragrant blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply cut foliage. Flowers range from single to fully double forms and make popular cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; cultivated in gardens throughout temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on sugary nectar.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, it blooms in late spring, carpeting streets with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Mediterranean, subtropical regions of California, Florida, Mexico, and Egypt
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacaranda trees earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City' and falling blossoms are said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Rhododendron macrophyllum
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with leathery leaves and large rounded trusses of bell-shaped flowers. It grows in the understory of coniferous forests and is the state flower of Washington.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid spring to early summer (April to June)
plants.location: Pacific Northwest of North America, from British Columbia to northern California
plants.funFact: Washington state chose this species as its state flower in 1892, when women voters selected it at the World's Fair in Chicago, even before they could vote in general elections.
